clue.text: In winter month that's hard, soldiers become cut off

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed in the middle of the month's abbreviation

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Troops stranded somewhere in a harsh December find themselves isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate or sever one thing from another is the same as to cut it off.

clue.text: Door-to door service offered by shop: save 50% on line

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

indicators.note: half of the word save is kept, its second two letters

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a railway line

explanation.surface: A shop advertises home drops alongside a half-price offer on a product line.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Door-to-door'. '50%' keeps VE, the back half of 'save'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing goods or post to each house in turn is a service of this name.

clue.text: Up-and-coming tailor stocking fashionable garment

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the whole assembly is read from the bottom upwards
the cut holds the trendy word inside it, as a stocking holds a leg

parts.note: to tailor cloth is to cut it
IN means trendy or in fashion

explanation.surface: A rising young tailor stocks a trendy item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The inner assembly, CINUT, is what 'Up-and-coming' turns round; in a down clue the reading runs upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose sleeveless body garment, often belted, is a classic article of clothing.

clue.text: About to swallow hot drink

indicators.note: the abbreviation for about takes the hot letter inside it

parts.note: CA abbreviates circa, Latin for about
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of gulping down a hot beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'nearly', but it is CA, which takes in H.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang word for tea, from Chinese, so a cup of it is a drink.

clue.text: Vehicle I parked at front of building suddenly disappeared

indicators.note: the first pieces are set down ahead of the building, so they come before it

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
taken as written
a shed is a small building

explanation.surface: A van parked outside a building and then vanished without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to pass out of sight all at once, so it means disappeared suddenly.

clue.text: The cost of travelling a long way in first class, extremely reasonable

parts.note: A1 means first class, the 1 read as I

indicators.note: the distance word goes inside the letters for first class and the ends of reasonable
only the extreme letters, first and last, of reasonable are used

parts.note: far means a long way

explanation.surface: Long-distance first-class travel turns out to be very reasonably priced.
explanation.walkthrough: FAR goes into AIRE, made of AI (A1) and RE, the outside letters of 'reasonable'.
explanation.definitionFit: The price of a ticket for a journey by plane is the fare one pays to travel.

clue.text: Indian people transfixed by first of these magic words

parts.note: the Inca were the native people of Peru, American Indians

indicators.note: pierced through, so the letter is driven into the word for people

parts.note: a nation is a people

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A tribe of Indians is spellbound by the first of some magic words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian people' wants to be one phrase; it splits into the tribe and a nation, and T comes from 'first of these'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell chanted aloud is a form of magic words.

clue.text: Man treated Albert to a drink

parts.note: a man is referred to as he

indicators.note: the letters are processed or worked on, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fellow makes Albert a soothing beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges ALBERT plus A into RBALTEA; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion of herbs such as camomile or mint is a hot drink.

clue.text: Decorate mug

definitions.meaning: to redecorate or refurbish a room
to beat up or attack someone

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to refurbish a room and, as slang, to assault someone violently.

clue.text: Don't pose as model without a blouse, for example

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the posing word wraps round the garment

parts.note: an artist's model is said to sit
a blouse is one kind of top

explanation.surface: Don't sit for the artist with your blouse off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' wants to mean 'not wearing'; here it is the old sense, outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'Don't!' to halt someone is the same as telling them to cease.

clue.text: Soldier guarding a street in northern city

indicators.note: the soldier surrounds and protects the other pieces

parts.note: a lancer is a cavalry soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is on guard on a street in a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: LANCASTER is a city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster, county town of Lancashire, is a city in the north of England.

clue.text: Get wretch to switch positions, a rare thing

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible person, a wretch
electrical switches mark their on and off settings with I and O

explanation.surface: Someone is told to make a scoundrel swap places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch positions' looks like an instruction to swap letters, but it is the I (on) and O (off) printed on switches. 'Get' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A curiosity is an unusual collectable object, prized for its rarity.

clue.text: Team member strangely inactive after accepting sporting honour

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the honour inside them
the letters are put in an odd new order

parts.note: a cap is awarded for playing for one's country

explanation.surface: A lazy player is nonetheless given an international honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges the fodder to VICETAIN before the honour goes in. A cap is given to a player picked for their country.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy to the skipper of a side is one particular player in it.

clue.text: Composer, first to consider stringed instrument, one for inclusion in record

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word consider is used

parts.note: a harp is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the word for record

parts.note: to enter data is to record it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A composer weighs up a stringed instrument for a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: Marc-Antoine CHARPENTIER was a French Baroque composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc-Antoine Charpentier wrote Baroque sacred music, and Gustave Charpentier wrote the opera Louise.

clue.text: Period piece nabbed by pillagers

indicators.note: a small piece of the following word is held inside it

explanation.surface: A piece from a historical era has been seized by looters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period piece' reads as one phrase, but 'Period' is the definition and 'piece' starts the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: An era or epoch of history is an extended period of time.

clue.text: Resume painting with support

parts.note: a rest is a prop or support
painting is an example of art

explanation.surface: Someone goes back to painting, with a prop to lean on.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade puts the support first, though the clue names it second; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin again after a pause is to resume.

clue.text: Chap at the helm terribly tense bearing arms awkwardly

indicators.note: carrying, so the first jumble holds the second inside it
the letters are badly arranged, so they are mixed up
the letters are placed clumsily, so they are mixed up too

explanation.surface: A helmsman, very tense, carries weapons in a clumsy way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' makes STEEN and 'awkwardly' makes RSMA; 'bearing' puts the second jumble inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmsman steers a vessel, so he is the man at the wheel.

clue.text: Bridge player needs hint about card game

indicators.note: turned about, so the word for hint is read backwards

parts.note: a trace is a slight hint or suggestion
E is East, one of the four bridge seats

explanation.surface: A bridge player needs a tip about a different card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TRACE into ECART; 'needs' is a link. Écarté is a two-player card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Écarté is a nineteenth-century card game for two players, using a short pack.

clue.text: Put down false name in legal document

indicators.note: the jumbled name sits inside the legal paper

parts.note: a deed is a legal document

indicators.note: the letters are not true to their order, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wrote a fake name on a deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' makes MEAN, which goes inside the document. 'Put down' is the verb: to belittle.
explanation.definitionFit: To humiliate or belittle someone is to put them down.

clue.text: Electronic device with buzzer's a bonus, mostly

parts.note: a bee is a buzzer; the 's is a link

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a perk is a bonus or extra benefit

explanation.surface: A device that comes with a buzzer counts as a welcome extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzzer' looks like part of the device, but it is the BEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager that bleeps to call its wearer is an electronic gadget.

clue.text: One style of music perhaps daily broadcast's taken up

parts.note: a rag is slang for a newspaper, a daily for example

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised up means read from the bottom

parts.note: to emit is to broadcast; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Some kind of music is perhaps adopted for a daily broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns EMIT into TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated piano style popular in early twentieth-century America.

clue.text: Forbidding one expression of disgust

parts.note: grim means forbidding or stern
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A stern refusal from one person is met with a look of distaste.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted facial look shows distaste or pain.

clue.text: At end of journey, gent fell asleep

indicators.note: the gentleman is placed at the end of the travel word

parts.note: to go is to journey
a toff is a well-to-do gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman dozed off when the trip was over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At end of journey' reads as a time phrase, but it is a placing instruction. TOFF is British slang for a posh gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: To drift into sleep is, in British idiom, to drop off or get off to sleep.

clue.text: Finished one's drink

parts.note: something past is over and finished
one is I, and the 's is read as is, together giving these letters

explanation.surface: Someone has finished their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: PASTIS is an aniseed-flavoured French aperitif.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastis is an aniseed-flavoured spirit from France, drunk with water.

clue.text: A short amount of time in Scottish town

parts.note: YR is the short form of year, a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone spends a brief spell in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: AYR is a town on the west coast of Scotland. 'short' signals the abbreviation, not a brief time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a coastal town in south-west Scotland.

clue.text: Heroic nurse's dash back to keep war leader away

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the other piece inside it
the word for dash is read backwards

parts.note: elan is dash or flair

indicators.note: the first letter of the war word is removed

parts.note: fighting is war

explanation.surface: A brave nurse hurries back to keep a military commander at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes NALE and 'leader away' makes IGHTING, which 'to keep' puts inside. Most solvers write it in from 'Heroic nurse' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence Nightingale nursed soldiers in the Crimean War and became a national heroine.

clue.text: One helping to catch black bear

indicators.note: the helper holds the colour letter inside

parts.note: an aide is an assistant, one who helps
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An assistant tries to catch a black bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb: to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with something is to abide it or bear it.

clue.text: Satisfied about front page in Times?

indicators.note: turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: requirements that are satisfied are met
the front page is page one, P1, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is pleased with the front page of the Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is musical speeds; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the plural of tempo means speeds or time markings, hence the question mark.

clue.text: What's not nice if spreading?

indicators.note: the letters spread out and rearrange like a contagion

explanation.surface: An unpleasant thing that spreads, as a riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of NOT NICE IF is the answer, and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A contagious illness is unpleasant, and it spreads from person to person.

clue.text: His work, to pursue crime principally

definitions.text: His work, to pursue crime principally

indicators.note: the work piece comes after, following behind
only the first, principal letter of the word is used

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A policeman's job is chiefly to chase criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a police officer's job, and its pieces build the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer's main job is chasing criminals.

clue.text: With heater, airs various items

parts.note: the sun heats the earth
to air laundry is to dry it

explanation.surface: Someone airs assorted bits and pieces with a heater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heater' looks like a household appliance, but it is the SUN; 'With' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous small articles.

clue.text: Lots of food shortages, of which the first's well over 2000 years ago?

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word shortages is used

parts.note: pre-AD means before the Christian era began, over two millennia back

explanation.surface: A huge banquet is set against shortages that go back to ancient times.
explanation.walkthrough: Split PRE-AD: before Anno Domini, so more than 2000 years ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a lavish array of dishes laid out for a meal.
